_about: Batch B1a (Basics I) glossary: learn/what-is-vllm, learn/openai-api, learn/processes-and-ipc, learn/python-entry-points, learn/pytorch-for-serving. Owner: the B1a writer.

v1-engine.short: The only engine of vLLM at this commit: the code in vllm/v1/ (AsyncLLM, the engine core, the scheduler, the workers). The old V0 names are aliases of it.

route.short: One HTTP method and path that the API server answers, for example POST /v1/chat/completions. FastAPI calls one handler function for each route.

entry-point-group.short: The name that collects related entry points in package metadata, for example console_scripts. Code asks importlib.metadata for all entry points of one group.
entry-point-group.long: vLLM reads its own groups, for example vllm.general_plugins. Those are the {{term plugin-group | plugin groups}}.

console-script.short: An entry point in the group console_scripts. The installer makes a small program with that name, for example vllm, that calls the given function.

torch-library-op.short: An operator that code registers with PyTorch under a namespace, for example torch.ops.vllm.unified_attention_with_output. torch.compile treats it as one opaque node.

fx-graph.short: A PyTorch data structure (torch.fx.GraphModule) that lists the operations of a function as nodes in order. Compiler passes read and change it.

dynamo.short: The capture part of torch.compile. It reads the Python bytecode of a function as it runs and records the tensor operations as an FX graph.

inductor.short: The default code generator of torch.compile. It turns an FX graph into fused kernels, for example Triton kernels on NVIDIA GPUs.

graph-break.short: A place where Dynamo cannot capture the Python code. Plain torch.compile then splits the function and runs that part in Python. vLLM compiles with fullgraph=True, so a break is an error.

zmq-socket-type.short: The pattern of a ZMQ socket, for example ROUTER, DEALER, PUSH, PULL or XPUB. The type sets who can send, who can receive and how messages are routed.

start-method.short: How Python's multiprocessing starts a child process: fork (copy the parent), spawn (start a new interpreter) or forkserver. vLLM reads it from VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD.
